root_cause.summary: One floating-point unit-in-the-last-place difference in a Person B synthetic U2 metric, which cascades into every downstream artifact hash in the report.
root_cause.explanation: 43 of the 44 differences are SHA-256 artifact hashes computed downstream of the single differing float. The checked-in fixture was generated on a host whose BLAS/libm produced the other last bit. Nothing in the report's structure, identities, counts, or statuses differs.

pre_existing.method: git stash push --include-untracked, re-ran the failing test at the pristine branch HEAD 35305576f67ba931cc464b8c3bae002b7d14d5dd, observed the identical failure, then git stash pop.
pre_existing.conclusion: The failure exists independently of every change made in this Person D sprint.

why_person_d_did_not_repair_it: The artifact is cross-role result-bearing evidence, not a Person D artifact. Regenerating it would overwrite a result-bearing artifact, which the provenance rules forbid.
The differing value is produced by Person B's synthetic analysis chain. Person D must not modify another role's scientific implementation.
Regenerating on this host would replace the recorded value with this machine's floating-point result, silently rebasing shared cross-role evidence onto one developer's BLAS build.
Adding a floating-point tolerance to the comparison would weaken a byte-exactness guarantee that Person D does not own.

options: Regenerate tests/fixtures/integration/synthetic_join_report.json on the canonical reference host and re-publish it as a versioned successor.
Or make the synthetic U2 metric bit-reproducible across BLAS builds (for example by fixing the reduction order) and then regenerate.
recommended_owner_action.person_d_dependency: none; no Person D output depends on this fixture

person_d_relevant_selection_impact.reason: Documented here and reported in the sprint's final status package. The Person D relevant selection is tests/baselines plus tests/contracts/test_analysis_inputs.py, both of which pass with zero failures.
